contexts.note: Full continuous source-first reading recorded in durable reports; parent checked canonical outcomes and introduced flags. UP348 self-critical inner-self rendering is held as a plausible contextual paraphrase of self-denigration, not certified as an independent agency defect. MG191 restores self as giver, with contextual unwillingness residual held. Other conservative candidates remain pending.

……彼女の尊い意思を、止める言葉などありはしない。
MG.translation: Ange sighed resignedly. ...No words would stop this girl's feelings of respect.

UP.japanese:
縁寿は眩暈を覚えたような仕草で溜息を漏らす。
……彼女の尊い意思を、止める言葉などありはしない。
UP.translation:
Ange sighed resignedly.
......She had no words with which to stop this girl from following her noble sense of purpose.

findings.sourceReading: 彼女の尊い意思 identifies her worthy determination to become the witch Father needs; it does not name reverence as the feeling Ange cannot stop.
findings.alternative: Her resolve is devoted to Father and may involve respect, but 尊い modifies the worth of her will rather than making respect its content.

findings.description: MG changes the self-granted right to love into having what it takes to fall in love.

contexts.japanese:
そんな自分に、もう二度と恋をする資格なんてないと思ってたッ！！」
「あるよ。
恋の資格はね？
自分だけが与えられるの。
家具だから駄目とか、そんなの関係ない。
駄目だって自分で決めたら、もう駄目なの。
決め付けちゃ駄目。
だから私は与えたよ、この身の程知らずな家具の身に、恋の資格を。
だから嘉音くんにだってあるよ」
「恋をする資格が？」

contexts.MG:
I believed that I didn't have what it takes to ever fall in love again!!"
"But that wasn't true.
Do you know what's needed to fall in love?
It's something you can't get from anyone but yourself.
Being furniture or not has nothing to do with it.
If you decide for yourself that it won't work out, then it won't.
You mustn't leap to such rigid conclusions.
That's why I, overambitious furniture that I am, gave myself what's needed to fall in love.
So you have it too, Kanon-kun."
"You mean, I have what it takes to fall in love?"
contexts.UP:
I believed that I didn't have any right to fall in love ever again!!"
"But you do.
The right to love...
is something only you can give yourself.
Being furniture or not has nothing to do with it.
If you tell yourself "no", then it'll never happen.
You mustn't think that way.
That's why I gave myself, impudent furniture that I am, the right to fall in love.
And you have it too."
"The right to fall in love?"

MG.japanese:
「悲しかったッ！！　自分につく嘘が、こんなにも辛くて悔しくて悲しいなんて知らなかった！！　そして僕のそんな嘘が、お嬢様を傷つけたのが、堪らなく許せなかった！！　そんな自分に、もう二度と恋をする資格なんてないと思ってたッ！！」
「あるよ。恋の資格はね？　自分だけが与えられるの。家具だから駄目とか、そんなの関係ない。駄目だって自分で決めたら、もう駄目なの。決め付けちゃ駄目。だから私は与えたよ、この身の程知らずな家具の身に、恋の資格を。だから嘉音くんにだってあるよ」
「恋をする資格が？」
MG.translation:
"I was!! I never realized that a lie you make to yourself could be so sad, so painful, so excruciating!! And I couldn't forgive myself for hurting Milady with that lie!! I believed that I didn't have what it takes to ever fall in love again!!" 
"But that wasn't true. Do you know what's needed to fall in love? It's something you can't get from anyone but yourself. Being furniture or not has nothing to do with it. If you decide for yourself that it won't work out, then it won't. You mustn't leap to such rigid conclusions. That's why I, overambitious furniture that I am, gave myself what's needed to fall in love. So you have it too, Kanon-kun." 
"You mean, I have what it takes to fall in love?"

findings.sourceReading: JP repeats 恋の資格 as a right one grants oneself. Original WH uses deserve and right; UP retains that entitlement. MG repeatedly uses what it takes and what is needed, shifting moral permission to personal capacity.
findings.alternative: What it takes can broadly include confidence or self-permission, but this repeated formulation removes the explicit entitlement under discussion.

findings.description: MG substitutes 音 for 嘉 in Jessica’s guess about Kanon’s real name.

contexts.japanese: きっと、嘉音の嘉が含まれた名前だと思うな…。
contexts.japanesePS3: きっと、嘉音の嘉が含まれた名前だと思うな…。
contexts.MG: I'll bet it has the character 音 in it, like Kanon does...
contexts.UP: I'll bet it has {ruby:ka:嘉 in it, like Kanon does...

MG.japanese: 「うん、今はそれでいい。だから私も、嘉音くんのこと、名前で呼びたい。……嘉音じゃなくて、……本当の名前があるんでしょ？　きっと、嘉音の嘉が含まれた名前だと思うな…。な、何だろ、……えへへ…」
MG.translation: "Good, that'll do for now. And I'd like to call you by your name, Kanon-kun. ...You have a real name...besides Kanon, don't you? I'll bet it has the character 音 in it, like Kanon does... Wh-What could it be, ...heheh..."

UP.japanese: 「うん、今はそれでいい。だから私も、嘉音くんのこと、名前で呼びたい。……嘉音じゃなくて、……本当の名前があるんでしょ？　きっと、嘉音の嘉が含まれた名前だと思うな…。な、何だろ、……えへへ…」
UP.translation: "Yeah. That'll do for now. And I'd like to call you by your name, Kanon‐kun. ......You have a real name...besides Kanon, don't you? I'll bet it has {ruby:ka:嘉 in it, like Kanon does... Wh‐what could it be, ......ehehe..."

findings.sourceReading: JP explicitly guesses 嘉 from 嘉音; original PC65637/65639 and UP retain 嘉. MG uses 音, changing the character she predicts.
findings.alternative: Both characters occur in Kanon, but only 嘉 is the source conjecture; no edition change licenses 音.

findings.description: MG inserts an extraneous to after will in Featherine’s command.

contexts.MG: you will to see to her needs."
contexts.UP: See that she has no trouble."

MG.japanese: 「面を上げよ、人の子よ。……その娘に、しばしの間、我が書庫を自由に閲覧する資格を与えようぞ。……我が巫女、縁寿。その方に世話を命ず」
MG.translation: "Raise your head, child of man. ...I shall give that child the privilege of using my library however she likes for a time. ...Ange, my miko, you will to see to her needs."

UP.japanese: 「面を上げよ、人の子よ。……その娘に、しばしの間、我が書庫を自由に閲覧する資格を与えようぞ。……我が巫女、縁寿。その方に世話を命ず」
UP.translation: "Raise your head, child of man. ......I shall give that child the privilege of browsing my archives as she pleases for a time. ......Ange, my miko. See that she has no trouble."

findings.sourceReading: MG you will to see to her needs is ungrammatical. JP commands Ange to care for Beatrice; original PC66298/66300 and UP use a grammatical imperative.
findings.alternative: The intended command remains recoverable; archaic diction does not license this construction.
